summary: Verdict: major problems. Most of the audit holds up. I checked these against the sources and reproduced them: the SCIP defaults, changelog lines and quotes; the ZIB 20-29 numbers; the BCM locators and the "deepest cut" remark; the CCDLM Thm 6.3 construction and its Ex 6.1 variant; the CWY theorem; the Eckstein-Nediak and Glover locators; the Theorem 14 corner facts (my own exact script); the Proposition B identity (my own sympy script); and the 0/47 and 0/73 cone-span counts (reruns gave identical output). The problems are in the comparison with Kilinc-Karzan-Yang (KY), which carries the revised verdict on Theorem 1 and Proposition 2, and in one unproved general claim. (1) The note misses KY Examples 4.2-4.5. Example 4.3 uses points (1-s, -s^2); Proposition 2(b) uses (-s^2, 1-s), so it is the same example with the coordinates swapped. KY already show that their strict condition cannot be dropped, and that attainment in the equality case depends on whether the points approach transversally or tangentially. So the claims "Prop 2(b) not found" and "Prop 2(b) shows the strict inequality cannot be dropped" are wrong, and the Theorem 1(4) novelty claim must be qualified. (2) KY Cor. 3.12 as printed is false: a D_2 point may sit on a ray that meets cl(B_2). KY's own Ex 4.3 and Prop 2(b) are counterexamples. The note says it uses the corollary "as stated", yet its Section 4.4 inference needs the corrected hypothesis. The Theorem 1(2) derivation itself survives. (3) Proposition B's general claim (C_F is neither a (14a) nor a (14b) set unless F is a positive multiple of a rotation) is proved only for F^T = diag(2, 1/2). A short lineality-space proof exists and is given in the review. Minor issues: the OpenCitations query for Munoz-Serrano 2022 used a wrong DOI. With the correct DOI there are 7 citers, all already known, so the conclusion is unchanged. Kilinc-Karzan-Steffy (Math. Program. 159, 2016) is missing. The statement "no published branch-and-bound comparison" is too strong, since the monoidal paper's computations and the Math. Program. 197 version were not read. Section 4.3 tests only part (1) of Proposition A; the conclusion still holds, because a bilinear S lies in no halfspace.

issues.location: note.md Summary item 1; Section 4.4 'The equality case'; Section 7 rows Thm 1(4), Prop 2(b); Section 8 item 1
issues.description: The note misses KY draft Examples 4.2-4.5 (pp. 21-23). Example 4.3 (B_2 points (1-s, -s^2) accumulating at the minimizer e_1, c = (1,1) not generated) is Proposition 2(b) with the coordinates swapped. KY already show that their strict condition cannot be dropped (Ex 4.3, 4.5). Ex 4.2 vs 4.3 already shows that attainment in the equality case depends on transversal vs tangential approach, which is the idea behind Theorem 1(4). The claims 'Prop 2(b) shows the strict inequality cannot be weakened' and 'Prop 2(b) not found as an example' are wrong priority claims. The Thm 1(4) verdict should be reduced to 'a general sufficient transversality condition'.

KY Cor. 3.12 as printed is false. D_2 is only required to avoid cl(B_2) pointwise, so a D_2 point may lie on a ray that meets cl(B_2) farther out. Counterexamples: KY's own Ex 4.3 with D_2 = {(1/2,0)}, and sfree Prop 2(b) with D_2 = {(0,1/2)}. The note says it assumes the corollary 'as stated', and infers that t*-sbar 'must be the D_1 representative' and that condition (iii) fails at the Theorem 14 corner. That inference holds only under the corrected hypothesis (the ray of each D_2 point avoids cl(B_2)), which is the one KY's proof uses. The derivation of Thm 1(2) survives under the corrected form; the note must state that form and why it is needed.

issues.location: note.md Section 5.2 Proposition B (last claim); code/check_bcm_orbit.py Part 3
issues.description: The general claim that C_F with det F > 0 and F not a positive multiple of a rotation is neither a (14a) nor a (14b) set is labeled proved, but is shown only for F^T = diag(2, 1/2); the script also prints a general conclusion from this one witness. The claim is true. Fix: lineality of C_A is A^{-1} span(J) and of C_G is G^{-1} span(J), so equality forces A = G/mu with mu > 0. The (14b) part is immediate, because (14b) sets lie in {ad <= bc} while int C_F lies in {det > 0}.

issues.location: logs/opencitations.log line 1; note.md Section 11 OpenCitations row
issues.description: Munoz-Serrano 2022 was queried with the invalid DOI 10.1007/s10107-021-01738-x, which returned 0 citers. The correct DOI 10.1007/s10107-021-01738-8 returns 7 citers, all already in the Section 2.1 table. The conclusion is unchanged, but the log and the '0-22 per DOI' row must be corrected and rerun.

Kilinc-Karzan-Steffy, Math. Program. 159 (2016) 585-605, is missing. It is refereed; KY's cone-case result restates its Prop. 5(b), and Yildiz's thesis says CWY was generalized there. It also proves sufficiency of relaxed CGFs without assumptions, which is close to Theorem 1(5). It should be compared and added to the must-cite list.

issues.location: note.md Summary 'Solver baseline', Section 6 'Correct baseline statement', Section 8 item 8
issues.description: 'There is no published branch-and-bound comparison' is stated flatly, but the monoidal paper's computations (which the SCIP 9 report cites for 'significantly outperform') and the Math. Program. 197 journal version were not read. It should say 'none in the sources I could read'.

Only part (1) of Proposition A (cone(P) = R^3) was tested, yet the note concludes that Proposition A applies to no corner studied. The conclusion is true, but the note should give the reason for part (2): {w <= xy} and {w >= xy} lie in no halfspace, while a cone other than R^3 lies in one, so parts (1) and (2) are equivalent here.
Only z_K < infinity is treated. The infinite case of Theorem 1(2) follows the same way (D_1 = empty set, since B ∩ cone(A) = empty set); add one sentence.
Theorem 1(4) is described as 'for C^1 quadratic constraints', but it is stated for any C^1 function q; adjust the wording.
